anomalies.observed: Net /NET0069 contains only the anodes of LEDs D21, D37, and D43; it has no supply, driver, or other component node. D19's anode, by contrast, is connected to +3V3.
anomalies.expected: Discrete LED anodes should be connected to a supply rail (e.g. +3V3) or an appropriate driven node so the LEDs can light. The netlist shows a floating common-anode net, which is not a normal functional connection.
anomalies.impact: D21, D37, and D43 cannot conduct and will remain dark; any status or Ethernet/activity indication they provide will not work.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U19 and U20 have both GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same system GND net. Their bus-side supplies are also not isolated from the logic-side ground.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN bus implementation, the transceiver's GND1 and GND2 should be separate grounds (or the design should use a non-isolated transceiver if isolation is not intended). The specification describes two isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of the CAN interfaces is defeated; the buses share the same ground as the logic side, removing the intended isolation benefit and allowing ground loops/common-mode coupling.

parsed.summary: The netlist supports at least one functional deviation: a common LED-anode net is floating with no supply, leaving D21/D37/D43 dark. A second likely deviation is that the isolated CAN transceiver grounds are tied together, contradicting the specified isolated CAN architecture.
